attempts.note: 5 deterministic rescores after this edit all produced the identical candidate=1696/dh=1820/matched_prefix=1 (no randomness in the toolchain, as expected -- confirms the number is stable, not noise). The tablejump theory (that forcing a dense switch would, on its own, widen the live set enough to fix the r8-r11 prologue) did NOT pan out: matched_prefix is measured from function entry, and the prologue's register-saving instructions are decided by GLOBAL register pressure across the whole function body, which is a property of how many DISTINCT values are simultaneously live across `bl` boundaries -- not of whether the dispatch mechanism happens to be a table vs a compare-chain later in the body. Read `bun tools/allocator-lens/lens.ts 080be378` (473 pseudos total) and alchemy-gcc/agscc/gcc/stmt.c's expand_end_case: the table-vs-chain decision and the prologue-shape decision are two independent compiler passes (stmt.c case expansion happens at tree-to-RTL time; local-alloc/global register class assignment happens later and is driven purely by live-range overlap counts). Root-cause hypothesis, now stronger: several sub-blocks in this draft are still simplified TODO stubs (L_080bee08's status/kind table, L_080bef28's status-cure gate, and critically Region_080bef88's real per-target power-accumulation loop at `.L_080bf0ca`) that in the true source reference `req`/`actor`/`abilityData`-equivalent values dozens of times each; my simplified stand-ins reference them only a handful of times, so the allocator finds it cheaper to reload from memory on demand than to dedicate 4 whole callee-saved registers for the function's duration. Finishing those specific remaining blocks (not further switch/table tuning) is the concrete next step most likely to move matched_prefix.
